/masood/lectures/masood-beg-2/.preservedPrefix: Study Long, Short, Market, Limit & Stop Orders.
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-2/.sourceTitle: LEC 2: What is Buy/Long & Sell Short in Trading? Complete Order Execution Guide
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-2/.sourceSummary: Mastering the operational mechanics of going Long (buying low to sell high) vs. Short (selling high to buy low), and when to use Market vs. Limit vs. Stop orders.
coreRules: Never use Market Orders to chase fast-moving green or red candles.
Every single trade MUST have a predetermined Stop Loss placed before order execution.

/masood/lectures/masood-beg-2/.takeaway: Distinguish a long position from a short sale and order types.

/masood/lectures/masood-beg-3/.sourceTitle: LEC 3: What are Trading Candlesticks? Anatomy, OHLC & Buying/Selling Pressure
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-3/.sourceSummary: Deconstructing the candlestick: Open, High, Low, Close (OHLC), the institutional truth behind candle bodies vs. wicks, and how to read displacement.
coreRules: A Market Structure Shift (MSS) or Break of Structure (BOS) is ONLY confirmed if the candle BODY closes beyond the swing level—a wick is just a liquidity sweep.
Observe where the candle body closes relative to its total range (top 20% = extreme bullishness; bottom 20% = extreme bearishness).
Small, alternating red/green candles signal consolidation; long directional candle bodies signal algorithmic delivery.
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-3/.takeaway: Read a candle's open, high, low, close, body and wicks.
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-3/.urduTakeaway: کینڈل کا اوپن، ہائی، لو، کلوز، باڈی اور وِکس پڑھیں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-beg-4/.sourceTitle: LEC 4: What is an Economic Calendar in Trading? Navigating Red Folders & High-Impact Events
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-4/.sourceSummary: Mastering the economic calendar (ForexFactory / Investing.com), decoding high-impact news releases, and protecting your capital from news volatility traps.
coreRules: Check the economic calendar every single morning at 07:00 AM NY time before opening any charts.
Abdullah Golden Rule: Never be in an active position 5 minutes before or 5 minutes after a Red Folder release.
Let the news candle sweep liquidity, create displacement, leave a clean Fair Value Gap, and trade the subsequent retest.
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-4/.takeaway: Locate high-impact economic releases on the calendar.

/masood/lectures/masood-beg-5/.sourceTitle: LEC 5: What is Trading Timeframe? Top-Down Multi-Timeframe Alignment & Fractality
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-5/.sourceSummary: Understanding the fractal nature of markets and building a systematic top-down routine from Monthly and Daily bias down to 5-minute and 1-minute entries.
coreRules: Always mark your key liquidity levels (Previous Day High/Low, Weekly High/Low) on the Daily chart before dropping to lower timeframes.
Only take 1-minute or 5-minute buy setups when the higher timeframe is seeking Buy-Side Liquidity (and vice versa for sells).
When higher timeframe and lower timeframe disagree, Higher Timeframe ALWAYS wins.
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-5/.takeaway: Separate higher-timeframe context from lower-timeframe execution.
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-5/.urduTakeaway: بڑے ٹائم فریم کے سیاق کو چھوٹے ٹائم فریم کی ایگزیکیوشن سے الگ کریں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-beg-7/.sourceTitle: LEC 7: What is Swing High & Swing Low? Fractal Structure, BOS & Market Structure Shifts
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-7/.sourceSummary: The exact mechanical definition of institutional swing highs and lows, identifying genuine structural breaks vs. liquidity sweeps, and avoiding fakeouts.
coreRules: Never eyeball random highs and lows; enforce the strict 3-candle rule.
An MSS requires aggressive candle displacement with an associated Fair Value Gap.
If price breaks a swing high with a wick only and instantly closes back below, it is a Liquidity Sweep, NOT a structure break!
/masood/lectures/masood-beg-7/.takeaway: Distinguish a wick beyond a swing from a closing-price break.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-4/.preservedPrefix: Study Consolidation After Large Price Moves.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-4/.sourceTitle: LEC 4: Never Trade After Big Moves! What is Consolidation in Trading? The Expansion-Consolidation Cycle
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-4/.sourceSummary: Why huge 200+ point trend days are almost always followed by choppy, non-directional consolidation, and how to protect your profits from the inevitable post-expansion trap.
coreRules: If yesterday was a massive 200+ point expansion day, expect today to be a consolidation day.
On expected consolidation days, either take the day completely off or cut your normal position size by 75% and target small 10-15 point scalps.
Wait for price to break out of the consolidation range and displace before seeking trend continuations.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-4/.takeaway: Contrast a large expansion day with later consolidation.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-5/.sourceSummary: Calculating 5-day and 20-day Average Daily Range (ADR) to identify market exhaustion points and predicting explosive expansion from Inside Day setups.

When current daily range reaches 90%–110% of ADR, cease entering new trend-continuation trades and look to take profit.
When an Inside Day prints, mark its high and low as prime breakout liquidity targets for the subsequent session.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-5/.takeaway: Measure average daily range using high-to-low distances.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-6/.sourceTitle: LEC 6: Why Retail Support and Resistance Fails: Algorithmic Market Makers Explained
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-6/.sourceSummary: Exposing the retail myth of support and resistance lines, how institutional algorithms engineer double tops and bottoms, and why liquidity resting above resistance is the real target.
coreRules: Never place your stop loss right below an obvious retail support level or double bottom.
When you see a clean "triple top" or "double bottom," do not trade the bounce—anticipate the SWEEP of that level.
Wait for price to aggressively puncture the support/resistance level, absorb the stops, and show displacement in the opposite direction before entering.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-6/.takeaway: Compare a level excursion with opposite-direction displacement.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-7/.preservedPrefix: Study Supply, Demand & Order Block Definitions.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-7/.sourceTitle: LEC 7: Why Supply/Demand & Retail Order Blocks Don’t Work? Algorithmic Truths
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-7/.sourceSummary: The critical distinctions between retail supply/demand boxes and true institutional Order Blocks validated by displacement and Fair Value Gaps.
coreRules: An Order Block without an associated Fair Value Gap is INVALID.
Order Blocks are only valid for ONE clean retest (first mitigation); subsequent touches have exponentially lower win rates.
Candle bodies must respect the Mean Threshold (50%) of the Order Block—if a candle body closes through the 50% line, the Order Block is invalidated.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-7/.takeaway: Question how supply-demand boxes and order-block references are chosen.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-10/.sourceSummary: Reading the 1-minute tape in real time: tracking candle body closures, observing liquidity delivery from fair value gaps, and executing with surgical precision.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-11/.sourceSummary: Comprehensive deep dive into the Interbank Price Delivery Algorithm (IPDA): the deterministic mathematics of modern institutional price quotation.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-12/.sourceTitle: LEC 12: ICT “Seek and Destroy Profile” Live Prediction and Explanation
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-12/.sourceSummary: Recognizing and avoiding the most lethal retail market maker profile: the Seek & Destroy condition where both highs and lows are ruthlessly swept without directional follow-through.
coreRules: If the market sweeps the Asian High, then sweeps the Asian Low, and immediately reverses back into the middle of the range, declare SEEK AND DESTROY.
In Seek and Destroy conditions, close your charts immediately—do not attempt to scalp.
Wait for the following trading day when normal directional delivery resumes.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-13/.sourceSummary: Real-time live execution breakdown on NASDAQ (US100): pre-market level marking, waiting for the 09:30 cash open sweep, entering at the 1M FVG, and executing partial profits.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-14/.sourceSummary: The systematic, objective framework for determining the correct Daily Bias before the market opens: the 3-step filter of HTF Draw, Liquidity Sweeps, and Session Alignment.
coreRules: If the Daily chart is expanding toward Buy-Side Liquidity, your bias is strictly BULLISH—prohibit all short trades.
If the Daily chart is expanding toward Sell-Side Liquidity, your bias is strictly BEARISH—prohibit all long trades.
If the higher timeframe is trapped in the middle of a consolidation range without a clear draw, your bias is NEUTRAL—stand aside.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-14/.takeaway: Compare the daily liquidity objective with the chosen directional bias.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-14/.urduTakeaway: روزانہ لیکویڈیٹی کے مقصد اور منتخب بائس کا تقابل کریں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-15/.sourceTitle: LEC 15: How to Trade ICT High Resistance Liquidity Run (HRLR) vs Low Resistance Liquidity Run (LRLR)
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-15/.sourceSummary: Differentiating between Low Resistance Liquidity Runs (explosive, one-way trending days) and High Resistance Liquidity Runs (choppy, difficult grinding days) to protect capital.
coreRules: LRLR = Full position size (1% risk), wide targets, hold runners.
HRLR = 0.25% risk, take quick 10-15 point scalps, or do not trade at all.
Look for LRLR conditions immediately following a major HTF liquidity sweep and displacement.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-15/.takeaway: Compare opposing PD arrays along high- and low-resistance paths.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-16/.sourceSummary: Tactical survival manual: identifying the early-warning signatures of a chop day within the first 20 minutes of the session and executing capital protection protocols.
coreRules: Never trade more than 2 setups in a single session.
If your first trade gets stopped out in chop, step back and re-evaluate whether the market is in Seek & Destroy.
A zero-trade day is a WINNING day when the market is distributing losses to retail.
/masood/lectures/masood-adv-16/.takeaway: Reassess a stopped trade when the session becomes two-sided.

/masood/lectures/masood-adv-20/.sourceSummary: Mastering the institutional Premium / Discount (P/D) Array hierarchy: Order Blocks, Fair Value Gaps, Breakers, and Mitigation Blocks mapped to the 50% Equilibrium rule.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-1/.sourceSummary: Mastering the Weekly Candle Profile: how the weekly candle’s Open, Low, High, and Close shape individual daily bias from Monday through Friday.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-6/.sourceTitle: LEC 6: ICT Volume Imbalance, Seasonal Tendencies & Daily Bias Shift
/masood/lectures/masood-db-6/.sourceSummary: The subtle but powerful mechanics of Volume Imbalances (body-to-body gaps), seasonal institutional tendencies, and identifying when the daily bias formally shifts.
coreRules: Mark every Volume Imbalance on your chart with a shaded box; treat it with the same respect as a Fair Value Gap.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-7/.sourceTitle: LEC 7: ICT IPDA Data Ranges (20, 40, 60 Day Lookback) & Liquidity Voids
/masood/lectures/masood-db-7/.sourceSummary: How the Interbank Price Delivery Algorithm references historical 20, 40, and 60-day institutional lookback windows to find liquidity voids and key price targets.
coreRules: Count back 20, 40, and 60 daily candles from the current day and mark the highest high and lowest low.
When price approaches a 20-day or 40-day high/low, anticipate major institutional profit-taking or reversal.
Liquidity voids must be filled before the market can establish sustainable new trends.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-7/.takeaway: Mark the highs and lows of 20-, 40- and 60-day lookbacks.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-7/.urduTakeaway: 20، 40 اور 60 دن کے سابقہ ریکارڈ کے ہائی اور لو نشان زد کریں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-db-8/.preservedPrefix: Study Trading Bias: Building a Conditional View.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-11/.sourceTitle: LEC 11: Intermarket Relationship: DXY vs US Indices vs EUR/USD

/masood/lectures/masood-db-12/.sourceTitle: LEC 12: ICT Algorithmic Price Delivery Continuum: The Perpetual Market Loop
/masood/lectures/masood-db-12/.sourceSummary: Understanding the perpetual 4-stage algorithmic cycle: Consolidation -> Expansion -> Retracement -> Reversal, and positioning yourself on the right stage of delivery.
coreRules: Never buy during an Expansion—wait for the Retracement phase.
Enter on the Retracement into the 50% equilibrium discount of the expansion leg.
Exit your trade during the subsequent Expansion into resting Buy-Side Liquidity.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-12/.takeaway: Distinguish consolidation, expansion, retracement and reversal phases.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-12/.urduTakeaway: کنسولیڈیشن، توسیع، واپسی اور پلٹاؤ کے مراحل میں فرق کریں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-db-13/.sourceTitle: LEC 13: Deep Dive Into ICT Liquidity & Inefficiency: BSL, SSL & Imbalances
/masood/lectures/masood-db-13/.sourceSummary: Comprehensive forensic study of Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL), Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL), and market inefficiencies (FVGs): the dual engines of institutional order flow.
coreRules: Always identify whether the nearest resting liquidity pool is BSL or SSL before looking for entries.

Combine liquidity sweeps with Fair Value Gap inefficiencies for highest-probability setups.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-13/.takeaway: Connect a liquidity sweep with the subsequent imbalance reference.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-13/.urduTakeaway: لیکویڈیٹی سویپ کو بعد کے عدم توازن کے حوالے سے ملائیں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-db-14/.sourceTitle: LEC 14: ICT Lower Timeframe Entry Technique With Daily Bias
/masood/lectures/masood-db-14/.sourceSummary: The exact multi-timeframe stepping stone: transitioning from Daily Bias to 15-minute structural framing down to 5-minute/1-minute execution within New York macro windows.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-14/.urduTakeaway: چھوٹے ٹائم فریم کی انٹری کو ڈیلی بائس کے سیاق سے ملائیں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-db-15/.preservedPrefix: Study SMT Divergence: Smart Money Technique.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-15/.sourceSummary: Unmasking institutional accumulation and distribution via intermarket correlation cracks between US100 (NASDAQ) and US500 (ES) or EURUSD and DXY.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-16/.sourceTitle: LEC 16: Mastering Market Traps: Engineered Liquidity & Fake MSS
/masood/lectures/masood-db-16/.sourceSummary: Exposing institutional trap mechanics: engineered retail inducement, fake market structure shifts, and turtle soups designed to liquidate early breakout traders.
coreRules: Always wait for the candle to officially CLOSE before confirming an MSS.

Never enter on the first breakout of a tight consolidation range; wait for the fakeout sweep, then trade the real move.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-16/.takeaway: Contrast a wick-only swing breach with a confirmed MSS reading.
/masood/lectures/masood-db-16/.urduTakeaway: صرف وِک سے سوئنگ پار ہونے اور تصدیق شدہ MSS کی تشریح کا تقابل کریں۔

/masood/lectures/masood-db-17/.sourceTitle: LEC 17: Master Tape Reading: Learn How to Read Order Flow (ICT MMXM)
/masood/lectures/masood-db-17/.sourceSummary: Decoding Market Maker Models: the Market Maker Buy Model (MMBM) and Market Maker Sell Model (MMSM), tracking the curve from original consolidation to smart money reversal and distribution.
coreRules: Identify the Original Consolidation level—this is the final profit target of the entire model.
Enter on the first re-accumulation/redistribution FVG after the Smart Money Reversal has formed.
Do not fight the curve: if the market is on the Buy-Side curve, only take long positions.

/masood/lectures/masood-db-19/.sourceTitle: LEC 19: Read the Tape Like Wall Street Traders: Real-Time Order Flow & Tape Reading Discipline
/masood/lectures/masood-db-19/.sourceSummary: Wall Street institutional tape reading: decoding candlestick speed, displacement signatures, volume absorption, and recognizing when smart money steps on the gas.

Follow the closing prices of candles rather than the high/low wicks.
